column1: # Architecture-check baseline. Generated by `sbt writeArchitectureBaseline`.
# Targets: method <= 80 lines, file <= 600 lines, no forbidden imports or calls.
# This list may shrink, never grow. Removing an entry is the point.
# Growth must be justified: CI fails a PR that grows this file's entry count or total measured
# lines/hits unless the same diff adds a '# paydown: <why, issue link>' comment line (see #1413).
# Columns: path <TAB> detail <TAB> measured
# paydown: +1 line each on LineWrappingSpec and ReplaceWorkflowStateManagerSpec for the StateManagerTestFacade
# import after moving test-only facade members out of production (#1692); offset by StateManagerCapabilitySpec
# shrinking 642 -> 636 as its test doubles lost those members, so the baseline total drops.
# paydown: LspManager.scala grew by 5 lines fixing #1507 -- replacing the placeholder `anchor: CursorPosition` on
# `startRequest`/`RequestContext` with a `RequestAnchor` ADT distinguishing cursor-anchored from whole-document
# requests, which needed a small enum plus accessor.
# paydown: LspManager.scala grew by another 36 lines adding textDocument/references and textDocument/rename (#1467)
# -- two more RequestKind cases dispatched through the file's existing startRequest/isCurrent/noServerEvent pattern.
# The request-building logic itself (the bulk of what these two methods needed) was extracted to a new file,
# LspManagerReferenceRenameSupport.scala, rather than left inline; what's left in LspManager.scala is the same
# per-RequestKind wiring every other kind already has here (RequestKind case, handleEffect dispatch case,
# noServerEvent case), which isn't reasonably splittable without breaking that existing pattern.
# paydown: GutterAndLineNumbersSpec.scala grew by another 1 line (636 -> 637) for the same reason as the #1692 entry
# above -- its bufferManager.createBuffer call sites move onto StateManagerTestFacade's createBuffer extension
# (#1724), needing the facade's import alongside the existing StateManager one.
# paydown: StateManagerCapabilitySpec.scala grew by 1 line (636 -> 637) resolving this PR's merge conflict with
# #1729's commandExecutor deletion -- both PRs edited the same capability-composition assertion, and the merged
# version names every capability retired by #1724 (paneManager/panelManager and commandExecutor) in one comment
# rather than two overlapping ones.
# paydown: issue #1669's remaining follow-up (this PR) moves `MarkdownPreviewWindowAvailability` out of
# `com.serenity.ui.tui` into `com.serenity.frontend` and onto `Frontend.markdownPreviewWindow`, exactly the fix this
# file's own comment (removed here) said was the way to close the 8 entries #1739 grandfathered for
# `StateManager`/`StateManagerComposition`/`StateManagerCapabilityPorts`/`StateManagerRuntime`/
# `StateManagerPanelEffects` threading that TUI-only type in directly. All 8 are gone: those files now hold a
# frontend-neutral type, so the `com/serenity/state` ForbiddenImports rule no longer fires on them at all.
# paydown: issue #1677 (steps 1-2, #1732/78fb6fa8c/61dc64278) threaded an explicit `RenderCaches` bundle (and
# instance-scoped `MarkdownPreviewCache`/`DictionaryCache`) through the whole render, mouse-hit-testing, and
# markdown-preview call graphs, replacing several JVM-wide singleton caches. That threading is an added parameter (or
# an added `caches: RenderCaches` construction) at nearly every call site it touches, which is why `CharacterRenderer`,
# several renderer/markdown specs, `PerformanceBenchmarks`, `RendererPaneContent`, `SpellCheckerSpec` and
# `TerminalRenderSurfaceSpec` all grew: the two `StateManager`/`StateManagerRuntime` line-number shifts below (185/186
# -> 191/192, 144 -> 146) are the same threading moving the existing `#1669` forbidden-reference hits down a few lines,
# not new instances of that violation. This step (step 3) only reconciles the baseline for that already-landed growth;
# it does not itself add any of this threading.
# paydown: issue #1677 step 3 adds an `ArchitectureChecks` rule forbidding `AtomicReference`/`AtomicInteger`/
# `synchronized`/`mutable.` inside a top-level `object` (anywhere in `src/main`) or anywhere under `state/models`
# (`state/models` itself has zero violations under this rule, so no baseline entries are needed for it -- steps 1-2
# already made it clean). The 13 entries below are every top-level-object hit the rule finds elsewhere, and every one
# is contained, per-call or per-constructed-instance mutation, not a JVM-wide singleton this issue asks to remove:
# `RendererCursorOverlay`/`RendererEntryPoints`/`RendererFramePlanner`/`SwingFileDialog` each create a fresh
# `AtomicReference` local to one render/dialog call, used only to carry a value out of a synchronous Swing/AWT
# callback within that same call, and discarded once the call returns -- the same "contained, local mutation ...
# StringBuilder during rendering" exception docs/coding-standards.md already grants, just holding a box instead of a
# builder. `RuntimeDisplayState`/`TerminalInputHandler`/`TuiRuntime`/`MarkdownPreviewWindow` each construct exactly
# one `AtomicReference` inside an `object`'s factory method (`apply`/`resource`/`run`) to seed the one new instance
# (or one bootstrap invocation) being built there -- the field ends up owned by that single instance/invocation, not
# shared JVM-wide, textually inside the `object` only because Scala's `object`-based smart-constructor idiom puts
# factory methods there. `HunspellFreeCompoundMatcher`'s `mutable.Map` is already documented in place as "Local,
# contained mutation ... matching this project's Mutation Policy". None of these was a cache issue #1677 asked to
# scope to an owning instance -- the one hit that was (`MouseTargetLayoutKey`'s single-slot `AtomicReference` memo,
# `state/manager/MouseTargetCache.scala`) has been moved onto a new instance-scoped `MouseTargetLayoutKeyCache` owned
# by `AuthoritativeUiScene` as part of this same step, and is not baselined here.
# paydown: StateManagerCapabilitySpec.scala grew by 1 line (638 -> 639): `CommandEffectInterpreter.Dependencies` gained
# `unrecordedCommand` (the `AppEffect.ExecuteCommandUnrecorded` route picker previews and dismiss commands take), and
# this spec's effect-order test builds every dependency by name.
# paydown: PerformanceBenchmarks.scala grew by 1 line (764 -> 765): `main` opens a second, laptop-sized window for
# LaptopFrameBenchmarks' present benchmark (#1798 follow-up). The benchmarks themselves live in their own file and the
# name-prefix selection in BenchmarkRunner.runMatching; what's left here is the one extra resource acquisition.
